page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.n1.3xlarge is an x86_64 virtual machine instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. The instance configuration provisions 16 virtual CPUs across 8 physical cores via hyperthreading, paired with 32.0 GB of system memory. This establishes a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The hardware architecture incorporates a 33 MB L3 cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache per core, and hardware instruction support including AVX, AVX-512, BMI2, and AES-NI. The instance contains zero local storage and no dedicated hardware accelerators, relying entirely on networked storage volumes.

Benchmark results demonstrate moderate multithreaded capacity set against restricted single-core compute. Synthetic testing yields a Geekbench multi-core score of 6,692.0 and a stress-ng multi-core metric of 15,839.14, placing the instance squarely in the middle 50% tier. Conversely, single-thread benchmarks expose legacy per-core throughput, reflected in a Geekbench single-core score of 936.0 and stress-ng single-core result of 1,106.89. PassMark database operations reached 4,290.01, while Redis SET throughput sustained 21.48 million operations per second.

Given its compute-heavy core density and lack of bundled local NVMe storage, the instance presents balanced resource allocation for distributed, parallelized tasks rather than latency-critical, single-threaded applications. The primary performance limitation is single-thread speed alongside modest memory bandwidth relative to newer platforms. The ecs.n1.3xlarge is suited for horizontally scaled web serving, software compilation clusters, background batch workers, and intermediate data processing pipelines.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.n1.3xlarge is a compute-focused x86_64 instance configured with 16 vCPUs (8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading) and 32.0 GB of RAM, providing a 1:2 compute-to-memory profile. Driven by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz with a 33 MB L3 cache, the system supports AVX-512 and AES vector operations. It provides no onboard local disk storage and contains no discrete GPUs, operating completely with networked storage. Benchmark data reflects average multi-core throughput, with a PassMark CPU score of 16,949.88, a Geekbench multi-core result of 6,692.0, and 21.48 million Redis SET operations per second, contrasted with weaker single-core performance. The instance serves cost-conscious parallel batch workloads, web application fleets, Clang compilation jobs, and general distributed compute pipelines.
